clue.text: One is posted during watch, for instance, as helmsman

indicators.note: something posted during a period is stationed inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a watch is an example of a timer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor on watch duty is stationed at the wheel as the ship's helmsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like a nautical shift, but with 'for instance' it means a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A timoneer is an old word for the sailor who steers, from the French for rudder.

clue.text: Duck out of business meeting

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone ducks out of a tedious business meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck; this spelling is a recognised variant name for the bird.

clue.text: County discard is hit with club

parts.note: to shed is to cast off or discard

explanation.surface: Someone working for a county council is beaten with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy bludgeon, so to be struck with one is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Plan for fast plane, including maximum speed

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: the plane word takes in the speed letter, holding it within

parts.note: a jet is a fast aircraft
c is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light, the fastest possible

explanation.surface: A scheme for a fast aircraft built to reach top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: c, the speed of light, is the universal speed limit, hence 'maximum speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A project is a planned undertaking, and as a verb to project is to plan ahead.

clue.text: My bad term of Latin

definitions.meaning: slang for admitting a mistake, 'my fault'
a Latin phrase meaning 'through my fault'

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a poor grasp of a Latin term.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin confession phrase translates literally as 'through my fault', which is what modern slang apology says.

clue.text: Additions to petrol mix can stink, OK?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase before it are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A garage hand asks whether the stinking fuel blend is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiknock agents, such as lead compounds once were, are fuel additives that stop engine knocking.

clue.text: River in East — that's crossed by crews

indicators.note: the crews word goes across the compass letter, lying either side of it

parts.note: gangs are working crews
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An eastern river that boat crews regularly cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India, flowing east to the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Record mostly minor changes in style of pictures

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a file is a record

indicators.note: the word minor changes its letter order

explanation.surface: A note that small shifts in film style were mostly recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a genre of dark, cynical crime movies, and pictures is an informal word for films.

clue.text: Set of nine or ten one had initially cut (an exception to theme among across solutions)

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its opening letter, the initial being cut away

explanation.surface: A query whether a group held nine or ten, one having been cut at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a comment: every other across answer holds three consecutive alphabet letters (MNO, NOP, HIJ, DEF...), and this one does not.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennead comes from the Greek for nine and names any group of nine, such as the nine Egyptian gods.

clue.text: School activity cancelled? On the contrary

parts.note: a notice reading 'no' something says it is off
PE, physical education, is a school lesson

explanation.surface: A question whether a school activity has been called off, met with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No PE' is how a notice would say that games were cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual flat refusal, a contradiction of what was suggested.

clue.text: Knave sharing 25% with top man in his hostile takeovers

indicators.note: the card words go in the possessive, sitting within it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the two card words share one letter where they meet, so it is written only once

parts.note: the jack is the knave in a card pack
the king is the top man in a court of cards or a realm

explanation.surface: A rogue grabs a quarter-share alongside the boss in his aggressive buyouts.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK and KING share their K, so JACKING is written with the letter once.
explanation.definitionFit: Hijacking a vehicle or a firm means seizing control of it by force, a hostile takeover.

clue.text: Guard having mainly brave aim

indicators.note: the main part of the word is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: to brave a danger is to defy it
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A sentry whose purpose is chiefly courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend something is to protect or guard it from attack.

clue.text: Lose power, protected by coppers no longer? That's convenient

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: the coppers word surrounds the other, shielding it

parts.note: pence are copper coins
an engine or battery that dies loses its power

explanation.surface: A policeman, guarded by former coppers, loses his clout and finds it handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; here it means low coins, as in British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedience is the quality of being advantageous or handy, the property of something convenient.

clue.text: State of what's still left in river and loch

indicators.note: the side letter goes in the river name

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
Loch Ness is the Scottish lake

explanation.surface: The condition of whatever lies motionless in a river and a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmness is the quality of being still and undisturbed, the state described.

clue.text: In error, grip is changed for work on magazine, say

indicators.note: the letters that follow are put wrongly, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A grip has been altered by mistake on a gun magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'In error' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic design is the craft of laying out visual material, as in a magazine's pages.

clue.text: What's brewing, if unions organised

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Trouble is brewing if the workers form trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is a drink such as tea made by steeping leaves, the liquid that brews.

clue.text: Dog and another pet grabbing old white garment

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador dog

indicators.note: the pet word seizes the letter, holding it within

parts.note: a cat is another pet

explanation.surface: A dog and a cat fight over an old white garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab coat is the white overall worn by scientists and doctors.

clue.text: Sign about journey south for old craft

indicators.note: the star sign goes round the other letters

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
a go is a trip, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A signal about a southward voyage for an antique vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Argosies were large merchant ships of the Renaissance, sailing vessels of former times.

clue.text: Knowing about relative showing off

indicators.note: the knowing word wraps round the relative

parts.note: fly is British slang for shrewd, knowing
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A sly remark about a family member who loves to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY as an adjective means sharp or streetwise in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaunty describes someone ostentatious, given to parading themselves.

clue.text: Churned up, as field after one's removed quantity of soil

indicators.note: churned means the letters are stirred into a new order
the letter is taken away from the scrambled letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A field dug over, with one load of earth taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is part of the letters, not of 'Churned up'; 'after' sequences the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadeful is the amount of earth a spade lifts in one go.

clue.text: Circle in pub drinks certain wines

indicators.note: the round letter goes in the drinks word

parts.note: pints are the standard pub measure of beer
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A group of friends in a pub orders particular wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir, gris and blanc are grape varieties and the wines named after them.

clue.text: See 15
For practice session, fail as well after switching halves

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places

parts.note: a well that fails has run dry

explanation.surface: A rehearsal that also flops after a half-time change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as well' looks like 'also', but it means like a water well.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or trial before the real thing.

clue.text: One acts in emergency ward, finally, with duty nurse needing replacement

indicators.note: the letters need replacing in a different order
only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A duty nurse in the emergency ward needs someone to cover her shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One acts in emergency' is the definition dressed as hospital work: a stand-in actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy learns another actor's part to perform it if the lead cannot go on.

clue.text: What's at heart of 23, long ago in former times

indicators.note: only the central letters of the referenced answer are kept, its outer three on each side dropped

parts.note: the solution of 23 across

explanation.surface: What lay at the centre of an earlier answer in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic adverb meaning formerly, at an earlier time.

clue.text: Authentic German dramatist affected by Brexit?

indicators.note: Brexit read as 'BR exit': the letters for Britain leave

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright

explanation.surface: Whether a genuine German playwright suffered from Britain leaving the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: BR abbreviates Britain, so 'Brexit' becomes 'BR exits' the dramatist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German borrowing meaning genuine or typical.

clue.text: Shares taken back by limited company that goes to wall

indicators.note: the word is taken back, read from its end to its start

parts.note: cuts are shares, as in a cut of the profits
Co. abbreviates company

explanation.surface: Stock retaken by a firm which then goes bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to the wall' suggests business failure; here it is plaster applied to a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is fine plaster used to coat or decorate walls.

clue.text: Challenging puzzles — though apart from one hard one, oddly easy

indicators.note: the word is taken without the named letter

parts.note: H abbreviates hard, as on pencils; only one of the two goes
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Hard puzzles, though one tricky one was strangely simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughies are difficult problems, informally including hard crosswords.
